title: Cooperative scheduler integrates with continuous batcher and fragmentation-aware allocator
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce p99 latency and disk spill for multi-tenant workloads by coordinating eviction/compaction activity with the continuous batching scheduler and kernel-selection heuristics. This PR implements a cooperative scheduling protocol between the KV cache allocator and the continuous batcher so that eviction and compaction are deferred or rate-limited during critical batching windows; adds a fragmentation-aware allocator that prefers in-place allocation/compaction-friendly placements; and surfaces a lightweight kernel-hint to the runtime to avoid expensive gather kernels on heavily-fragmented segments. Changes are intentionally conservative: the cooperative protocol is opt-in per-tenant and disabled by default; the allocator uses a soft-reservation model to avoid hard failures; and we ship additional observability to validate behavior in staging. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2147) - [x] Unit tests for allocator invariants - [x] E2E perf bench against production trace - [x] Feature flag + rollout plan - [x] Documentation notes for ops and console UI Migration notes: no DB migration; new config keys added under runtime.kv.cooperative_scheduler and runtime.kv.fragmentation_profile; default preserves previous behavior. Rollout: staged canary on dedicated clusters for 48h then global rollout via feature flag.

ci_checks: Suite: linux-clang-unit (pass), linux-gcc-integration (flaky->rerun->pass), bench-regression (pass on canary infra), lint (warning free), type-checks (pass). One flaky integration test failed on first run due to test harness timing; addressed by increasing test timeout and re-running CI. Staging deployment smoke tests passed on 3/3 canary nodes.
benchmark_results: Bench run: production trace (24h shard) - baseline vs this PR: median latency +2% (small overhead), p95 -10%, p99 -18%, total disk spill events -22%, background compaction CPU increase +6% under heavy churn but net tail latency improvement. Memory reclaimed vs baseline under same workload: 14% reduction in spill bytes. Notes: numbers from bench/perf run on n1-standard equivalent canary cluster; results stable across 3 runs.
merge_outcome: merged via squash-and-merge after approvals; merge commit message summarizes cooperative scheduler API, frag-aware allocator, kernel hint plumbing, and benchmark summary. Rollout gated by feature flag and monitored via kv_fragmentation_rule alert.
release_notes: Improves p99 latency and reduces disk spill for KV-backed caches by coordinating eviction with batching windows and using a fragmentation-aware allocator. Opt-in feature; ops guidance in docs/ops/kv_cooperative_scheduler.md. Impact: lower tail latency for multi-tenant workloads and reduced I/O under contentious cache pressure. Backwards compatible; no data migration required.
